title: Without Kendrick Lamar — or Drake — How Will Hip-Hop Show Up In the Grammys’ Biggest Categories?
summary: Without an obvious star in contention — and given some of hip-hop’s declines in the past year — the genre’s marquee category chances may be slimmer.
body: “At the end of the day, nothing more powerful than rap music,” Kendrick Lamar said onstage at the 2025 Grammys. “We are the culture.” The Los Angeles rapper was accepting song of the year for “Not Like Us,” which won five awards that night, including record of the year. Lamar would return the following year to pick up another five Grammys for his GNX album and its smash SZA collaboration “Luther,” which made him the first solo male artist to win record of the year in consecutive years. And GNX was nominated for album of the year in 2026 alongside Tyler, The Creator’s Chromakopia and Clipse’s Let God Sort Em Out — only the second time three rap albums were up for that prize in the same year. Of late, hip-hop has had a starring role on Music’s Biggest Night — but 2027 could be different. As it has for much of the streaming era, hip-hop reigned supreme in 2026 as the most consumed form of popular music, leading all genres in streams. Look a little closer, however, and its chart dominance has been slipping for years. body: TL;DR Now On Wrist brings your Pixel’s Now Playing results directly to a Wear OS smartwatch. It can show detected songs through notifications, a watch face complication, and a dedicated Wear OS tile. The app is available now on Google Play and works with Wear OS 3.0 or newer. Hearing a great song and having your Pixel identify it automatically is handy, but checking the result still usually means reaching for your phone. That feels a little clunky when you’re already wearing a smartwatch, which is where a new app called Now On Wrist comes in. It fixes that disconnect by bringing your Pixel’s Now Playing results directly to Wear OS. Now On Wrist doesn’t actually turn your smartwatch into a music-recognition device. Instead, it relies on the ambient music recognition happening on your phone, including Google’s Now Playing feature, and sends the identified song and artist to your wrist.

title: This iOS calendar app is side-stepping Android to embrace Googlebooks
summary: Will we be seeing more Googlebook exclusives further down the road?
body: TL;DR Fantastical launched as an iOS calendar app 15 years ago. It’s now finally coming to Google’s mobile devices with a Googlebook port. There’s a free version available, as well as several premium paid tiers. In a perfect world, the software we want to use would be available across all major platforms — but that’s just not the reality we live in. For multiple reasons, access is still a problem, and we’re always happy to see when a developer opens its doors to a new platform. Most of the time, that’s an iOS-only app finally becoming available for Android phones . body: TL;DR Google says domestic flights have historically been cheapest around 39 days before departure, while international fares hit their lowest around 89 days out. The idea that Tuesday is the best day to book is largely a myth, with the cheapest booking day saving only about 1.4% versus the most expensive. Changing when and how you fly matters more: weekday travel can save up to 20% domestically, while nonstop flights cost around 20% more than connecting options. Booking a flight can sometimes feel like a gamble. You find a fare that looks reasonable, but instead of booking it, you start wondering whether it’ll be cheaper tomorrow. title: Lenovo Smart Clocks are finally getting their weather back
summary: No more having to check outside like a sucker!
body: TL;DR Across August and September, Lenovo Smart Clock Essential owners reported losing the weather display on their devices. Within the past 24 hours, weather suddenly seems to be retuning. Change can be hard for smart homes. While we love getting new features that make our smart home hardware better, far too often we hear about manufacturers abandoning old products , turning off necessary cloud infrastructure and leaving them worthless. Even when they don’t break something entirely, sometimes old functionality just up and vanishes — like we learned about last month with the Lenovo Smart Clock Essential. Thankfully, today we have some good news to share for a change. Lenovo’s Smart Clocks are a lot more restrained than a full-featured smart home display like a Nest Hub, and the display on the Lenovo Smart Clock Essential focused on just showing you the time — and the weather. But this past summer, users started noticing that the weather was disappearing from their Smart Clocks , leaving only the time behind.

title: YouTube is cleaning up one of the worst parts of Shorts
summary: Giving low-effort Shorts less room to breathe.
body: TL;DR YouTube is updating Shorts recommendations to prioritize original content and reduce the reach of low-effort reuploads from other creators. Reused clips can still surface if creators add meaningful commentary, editing, storytelling, or another original angle. For viewers, the change should make the Shorts feed feel less repetitive, while creators clipping their own long-form videos likely won’t be affected. YouTube Shorts have never exactly been a fan-favorite feature. From users wanting Shorts to be a standalone app, to YouTube itself letting users set their daily Shorts feed limit to zer o, there’s no shortage of signs pointing to how unhappy many users are with how aggressively short-form video has been pushed across the platform. One of the big reasons behind the disdain is the sheer amount of slop that floods the Shorts feed . YouTube knows that, and it is now starting to prioritize original content on Shorts. Announced by the streaming giant in a blog post this week, YouTube is updating its recommendation system specific to Shorts to reduce the reach of re-uploaded content, where videos taken from other creators are reposted without adding anything meaningful.

title: Chrome on Android’s password autofill could soon require a biometric test
summary: Revisiting an old idea.
body: TL;DR Google is testing biometric authentication before password autofill in Chrome for Android. The feature has returned in Chrome Canary after Google previously tested and pulled a similar implementation before stable release. The flag works for some users, but it didn’t trigger on a Pixel 8 in testing, suggesting the rollout is still limited or incomplete. Google Chrome on Android does a lot of heavy lifting when it comes to passwords. With Google Password Manager, the browser lets you seamlessly add and save new passwords, complete with the option to use strong suggested options. And when you return to a website where you’ve previously saved your login credentials, Chrome can automatically fill them in for you. As convenient as that is, Google wants to add an additional step to that process. Google is testing a new feature where Chrome on Android will require biometric authentication before it autofills passwords.
